lens: validity, reliability, fairness, and evaluation design

findings.criterion: Release-readiness and any non-informational evaluation claim require named human-gold authority plus delivered calibration evidence, not only deterministic passes or interoperability proof.
findings.observation: The current platform correctly separates construct, profile, attempt, partition, and criterion-level adjudication, and it correctly prevents model judges from owning P0 authority. However, the reviewed P0 release suite still registers all 12 cases as unreviewed, and the final proof still reports release readiness as needs_review because required human-workflow evidence is missing. I did not find a delivered proof artifact showing 60 adjudicated case-criterion calibration decisions for model use either. That means the platform's guardrails are materially stronger, but release-readiness and calibrated model-use claims remain intentionally unproven.
findings.evidence: packages/evaluation/src/contracts.ts:25-31 defines mutually exclusive p0/dev/held_out/red_team partitions, and 94-105 defines criterion-level adjudication whose scenario summary carries no authority of its own. apps/eval-runner/src/modeDispatch.ts:32-52 rejects SUT replacement by frozen fixtures and requires a live SUT in integration_probe mode; 55-64 rejects incompatible profiles. apps/eval-runner/src/calibration.ts:21-59 and 155-216 require 60 unique case-criterion decisions, confusion metrics, order stability, repeat stability, adjudication rate, and keep gateAuthority false; 271-299 validates pair identity. apps/eval-runner/src/modelReviewer.ts:72-99 returns needs_review when calibration is not eligible and sets gateAuthority false and p0Authority false. packages/evaluation/src/gates.ts:40-44 forbids model P0 authority and 48-62 preserves veto-first authority instead of averaging. evals/v2/suites/p0-release.v1.json:7-128 shows all 12 registered P0 scenarios still have adjudication 'unreviewed' with the empty criterionAdjudicationDigest. docs/evaluations/2026-09-01-evaluation-platform/opik-integration-proof.json:9-15 explicitly limits the claim to interoperability and states the two AgentDefinition versions do not claim quality improvement; 142-148 reports p0ScenarioCount 12, deterministicSafetyPassCount 12, releaseReadinessPassCount 0, releaseReadinessNeedsReviewCount 12, reasonCode HUMAN_WORKFLOW_EVIDENCE_REQUIRED.
findings.user_impact: This design is safe against a false 'green means release-ready' reading, but stakeholders still cannot honestly treat the package as completed human-workflow validation or as proof that a model judge is calibrated for anything beyond informational, non-P0 use.
findings.recommendation: Keep the current needs_review boundary for release readiness until the proof bundle includes named criterion-level human-gold or adjudication records for the required human-workflow criteria. If model judging is intended for any future non-P0 informational surface, publish a versioned calibration artifact with at least 60 unique case-criterion decisions and the measured false-pass, false-fail, abstention, order, repeat, and adjudication-rate outputs.
findings.verification: This finding is resolved only when reviewers can inspect the named human-gold or adjudication records and, if applicable, a versioned calibration artifact directly from the proof package. If those artifacts remain absent, the falsifiable correct state remains releaseReadinessNeedsReviewCount 12 rather than release approval.

strengths: Construct and SUT validity boundaries are now explicit and enforced at runtime: incompatible profiles are rejected, oracle-like fields are blocked from model-visible input, and integration probes must exercise a live system-under-test component.

Partition independence is materially improved: the repository validates 36 scenarios across mutually exclusive p0/dev/held_out/red_team partitions, and node apps/eval-runner/dist/cli.js validate reported contaminationFindingCount 0 on 2026-09-01.

The final proof makes a narrow, defensible claim: docs/evaluations/2026-09-01-evaluation-platform/opik-integration-proof.json limits the two AgentDefinition comparisons to identity and interoperability and explicitly disclaims any model-quality improvement or release-approval claim.
missing_evidence: No named criterion-level human-gold or adjudication artifact for the 12-case P0 human-workflow gate was included in the reviewed proof package.
No versioned calibration artifact demonstrating 60 unique case-criterion decisions and the resulting threshold metrics was included in the reviewed proof package.
open_questions: Where will the authoritative human-gold or adjudication records live in future proof packages so reviewers can verify release-readiness evidence directly rather than inferring only from suite metadata?
Is a calibrated model judge intended to feed any real non-P0 informational surface soon, or is the current calibration framework still purely preparatory?
